script: I was always there—now I am sick, and everyone vanished.. I was the friend who answered every 4 AM call, remembered every allergy, sent soup when you were freezing, texted "good luck" before exams, never missed a birthday. I didn't keep score. I was the caretaker. Then I got sick—not a terminal thing, but scary enough for surgery and weeks of home rehab. I pinged the group chat. "Let me know if you need anything," one friend said. I said, "Yeah, grab groceries, maybe sit with me so I don't feel lonely." They all said, "We'll check schedules." Still waiting. Three days post‑Original poster, a friend texts, "Are you still good to help me move next weekend?" Another posts brunch pics while I am stuck in bed, no food. No one checks on me. No one shows up. That's when I saw the truth: I wasn't their friend. I was their 24/7 concierge with a pulse. When I needed help, I disappeared. I stopped texting, didn't even say goodbye. I just went quiet. In that silence I reclaimed the energy I'd been giving away for years. I am not angry, just not available to people who treat my love like a utility. I wasn't a bad friend—I was a good one, just for the wrong people.
